items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2891

SPONSOR: SALAZAR
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the administrative code of the city of New York and the
emergency tenant protection act of nineteen seventy-four, in relation to
the duration of renewal leases; and to repeal certain provisions of such
laws relating to the increase in rent for such renewal leases

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this legislation is to provide residential tenants
already protected by the stabilization provisions of the New York City
Administrative Code or the emergency tenant protection act of 1974, as
amended, with the option of one, two, three or four year leases. Current
law only provides the option of one or two year leases.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one amends Section 26-511 (4) (c) of the administrative code of
the City of New York by requiring owners covered by the stabilization
provisions to grant three or four lease options to tenants in addition
to the already existing requirement of one or two year lease options.

Section 2 amends subdivision a of section 10 of section 4 of chapter 576
of the laws of 1974, constituting the emergency tenant protection act of
1974, as amended by chapter 234 of the laws of 1984, applicable to
cities having a population of less than one million and to towns and
villages, by requiring owners to grant three or four lease options to
tenants in addition to the already existing requirement of one or two
year lease options.

Section 3 provides that this Act will be effective immediately and
further provides that the amendments implemented in this Act shall
expire on the same dates that the underlying laws expire.

 
EXISTING LAW:

Existing law requires owners covered by the NYC Administrative Code
stabilization provisions and those covered by the emergency tenant
protection act of 1974 to grant tenants one or two year lease options.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

By requiring owners of to grant tenants three or four year lease options
in addition to the existing one- or two-year lease options this measure
provides protections to tenants to enhance the stability of housing
accommodations for themselves and their families. Current pricing of
rental housing and supply and demand variables have increased displace-
ment of individuals and families holding one or two year leases and
subjects them to possible homelessness and forces them to increasingly
unaffordable rents being charged for limited safe and adequate housing
stock.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This Act shall take effect immediately and further provides that the
amendments implemented in this Act shall expire on the same dates that
the underlying laws expire.

summary: Provides that tenants shall be offered the option of a one, two, three or four year renewal lease; repeals certain provisions relating to the increase in rent for such renewal leases.
